h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר כ״ז Pesach — Maamar Kaf Zayin
Achtriel in the Holy of Holies: "Bless Me" and the Throne of the Ancient of Days

p: בַּגְּמָרָא
In the Gemara
(בְּרָכוֹת ז'.):
(Berachos 7a):
אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: פַּעַם אַחַת נִכְנַסְתִּי לְהַקְטִיר קְטוֹרֶת לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים וְרָאִיתִי אַכְתְּרִיאֵל וְכוּלֵּי.
"Rabbi Yishmael said: Once I entered to offer incense in the innermost sanctum [the Holy of Holies], and I saw Achtriel, etc."
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
In the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' קכ"א.):
וְהַחָכְמָה מֵאַיִן תִּמָּצֵא — וְהַחָכְמָה מֵאֲתַר דְּאִיקְרֵי קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים נָפְקַת, מֵ"אַיִן" — עַתִּיקָא סְתִימָאָה דְּכָל סְתִימִין אִיקְרֵי "אַיִן"

"'And wisdom, from where (me'ayin) shall it be found?'—Wisdom emerges from the place called the Holy of Holies, from Ayin ('Nothingness'), for Atika, the most concealed of all concealed realms, is called Ayin"
(שָׁם ס"ד: וְאִדְּרָא זוּטָא הַאֲזִינוּ ר"צ:).
(ibid. 64b, and Idra Zuta, Ha'azinu 290b).
וְזֶה שֶׁהִזְכִּיר כָּאן שֵׁם שֶׁל כֶּתֶר: אַכְתְּרִיאֵל.
And this is why it mentions here a Divine Name associated with Kesser (Crown): Achtriel.
יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא וְכוּלֵּי
"Sitting upon a throne, etc."
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
based on what they said in the Midrash
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"ג, א'):
(Shemos Rabbah 23:1):
מִשֶּׁבָּרָאתָ אוֹתוֹ אַתָּה הוּא, אֶלָּא כִּבְיָכוֹל עוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵּי, נִתְיַשְּׁבָה מַלְכוּתְךָ וְכִסְאֲךָ נָכוֹן וְכוּלֵּי
"From the time You created the world You are the same, yet as it were You were standing [until we sang the Song at the Sea], etc.; then Your kingship became settled and Your throne established, etc."
וּכְתִיב
and it is written
(Daniel 7:9):
עַד דִּי כָרְסָוָן רְמִיו וְעַתִּיק יוֹמִין יְתִב.
"Until thrones were set in place and the Ancient of Days sat."
וּכְשֶׁקִּבְּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף, נַעֲשָׂה הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל:
And when Israel accepted His kingship, may He be blessed, at the Splitting of the Sea, the Sanctuary was established within the heart of Israel:
הָאָרֶץ הֲדֹם רַגְלָי, וְעַתִּיק יוֹמִין יְתִב, וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ נִקְרָא הֲדֹם רַגְלֵי אֱלֹהֵינוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַכּוֹת
"The earth is My footstool," and the Ancient of Days sat, for the Holy Temple is called "the footstool of our God," as they said in Makkos
וְשָׁם מְקוֹר כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת, דְּאִיתָא
And there is the source of all blessings, as it is stated
(מוֹעֵד קָטָן כ"ח.):
(Moed Katan 28a):
חַיֵּי, בְּנֵי, וּמְזוֹנֵי לָאו בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָין אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא,
"Life, children, and sustenance do not depend on merit, rather on supernal flow (mazala)"
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and it is stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' ע"ט:)
שֶׁהוּא עַתִּיקָא, מַזָּלָא קַדִּישָׁא.
that this is Atika, the Holy Mazal.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this is what is said
(שְׁמוּאֵל א' א', י'):
(I Shmuel 1:10):
וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל חַנָּה עַל הֲוָיָ"ה
"And Channah prayed upon (al) Hashem,"
הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה' יְהָבְךָ
and "Cast upon (al) Hashem your burden"
(תְּהִלִּים נ"ה, כ"ג)
(Tehillim 55:23)
"עַל" דַּיְיקָא, דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַתֵּשַׁע מִדּוֹת
specifically "upon/above" (al), for the Name Havayah encompasses all nine lower attributes
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' רנ"ח סוֹף ע"א)
(Zohar, Vol. 3, 258, end of amud a)
וְקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד דִּלְעֵילָּא רְמִיזָא לְ"אַיִן", כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
while the upper tip of the Yud above alludes to Ayin, Kesser Elyon
(שָׁם ס"ה:)
(ibid. 65b)
וְזֶהוּ "עַל הֲוָיָ"ה",
and this is "above Havayah."
וְכָל הַבְּרָכוֹת כְּלוּלִים בְּהָנֵי תְּלַת מִילֵּי:
And all blessings are encompassed in these three things [life, children, and sustenance]:
דְּמָצִינוּ בְּרָכָה דְּאָדָם וּבְרָכָה דְּדָגִים: פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ — בְּנֵי;
for we find the blessing of man and the blessing of fish, "Be fruitful and multiply"—which is children;
וּבְשַׁבָּת כְּתִיב
and regarding Shabbos it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית ב', ג'):
(Bereishis 2:3):
וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי,
"And God blessed the seventh day,"
וְאִיתָא
and it is stated
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה י"א, א'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 11:1):
בִּרְכַּת ה' הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר — זוֹ הַשַּׁבָּת,
"'The blessing of Hashem, it makes rich'—this refers to Shabbos,"
וּכְתִיב
and it is written
(שְׁמוֹת כ"ג, כ"ה):
(Shemos 23:25):
וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ וְגוֹמֵר — מְזוֹנֵי, וַהֲסִרֹתִי מַחֲלָה מִקִּרְבֶּךָ — הֲרֵי חַיֵּי,
"And He will bless your bread, etc."—which is sustenance—and "and I will remove illness from your midst"—which is life
שֶׁבְּכוּלָּם נֶאֱמַר לְשׁוֹן בְּרָכָה.
for in all of them the term "blessing" is stated.
וְאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנִי, בָּרְכֵנִי
And the Holy One, blessed is He, said [to Rabbi Yishmael]: "Yishmael My son, bless Me"
וְהַיְינוּ דְּתַכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה "בְּרֵאשִׁית" בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ רֵאשִׁית, שֶׁיְּקַבְּלוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ,
for the ultimate purpose of Creation—"In the beginning (Bereishis)"—was for the sake of Israel, who are called "First" (Reishis), so that they would accept the yoke of His kingship,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר "בָּרְכֵנִי": לְהַמְשִׁיךְ הַבְּרָכָה מִמְּקוֹר הַבְּרָכָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
and this is what He meant by "Bless Me": to draw down blessing from the Source of all blessing to Israel.
וְאָמַר לוֹ: יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁיִּכְבְּשׁוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ אֶת כַּעַסְךָ וְכוּלֵּי.
And Rabbi Yishmael said to Him: "May it be Your will that Your mercy suppress Your anger, etc."
וְכִלְשׁוֹן הַזֶּה אָמַר בַּגְּמָרָא לְעֵיל מִינֵּה:
And in this very same phrasing the Gemara says just earlier [on that page]:
תְּפִלָּתָם לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּתִי, שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְפַּלֵּל; מַאי מְצַלֵּי? יְהִי רָצוֹן וְכוּלֵּי
"It does not say 'their prayer,' rather 'My prayer,' teaching that the Holy One, blessed is He, prays. What does He pray? 'May it be My will, etc.'"
כִּלְשׁוֹן הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן מִתְפַּלֵּל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ.
using this exact same formula, Hashem, may He be blessed, also prays.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this is what is said
(תְּהִלִּים ק"ג, א'):
(Tehillim 103:1):
לְדָוִד בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת ה'
"Of David: Bless, O my soul, Hashem"
שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה עִם תָּגוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד כּוֹלֵל כָּל עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת;
for the Name Havayah together with the upper crown-tip of the Yud encompasses all ten Sefiros;
וְכָל קְרָבַי אֶת שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ
"and all my inward parts [bless] His holy Name"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
along the lines of what they said
(תַּעֲנִית י"א:):
(Taanis 11b):
כְּאִילּוּ קָדוֹשׁ שָׁרוּי בְּתוֹךְ מֵעָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"It is as though the Holy One dwells within his innards, as it is said
(הוֹשֵׁעַ י"א, ט'):
(Hoshea 11:9):
בְּקִרְבְּךָ קָדוֹשׁ וְגוֹמֵר.
'In your midst is the Holy One, etc.'"
וּבְשַׁבָּת כָּל הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִיזַ"ל שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת אַף אִם אוֹכֵל לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
And on Shabbos all bodily pleasure is imbued with holiness, as the Arizal wrote that on Shabbos even if one eats for his own enjoyment it is likewise in holiness,
וּבְשֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ
and in the Shulchan Aruch
(אוֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן ש"א סְעִיף ב')
(Orach Chaim 301:2)
שֶׁהַמִּתְעַנְּגִים בִּקְפִיצָה וְכַדּוֹמֶה גַּם כֵּן מוּתָּר בְּשַׁבָּת.
that those who take pleasure in running and jumping and the like are also permitted to do so on Shabbos.
וְכָתוּב: אֶת שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ
And it is written "His holy Name"
וְשֵׁם הַיְינוּ שֵׁם אֲדֹנָי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ תְּפִיסָה, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא "שֵׁם", כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
for "Name" refers to the Name Adonai [Malchus], which is graspable and is therefore called "Name," as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' קל"ד רֵישׁ ע"א),
(Vol. 2, 134, top of amud a),
וְרֹאשׁ הַפָּסוּק: בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת הֲוָיָ"ה,
whereas the beginning of the verse states "Bless, O my soul, Havayah."
אַךְ חָכְמָה עִילָּאָה אִיקְרֵי קֹדֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר
However, Supernal Wisdom (Chochmah Ila'ah) is called "Holy" (Kodesh), as brought in the Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' רצ"ז רֵישׁ ע"א),
(Vol. 3, 297, top of amud a),
וְ"שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ" הַיְינוּ שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְ"שֵׁם" הַיְינוּ הַתְּפִיסָה
so "His holy Name" refers to the Name Havayah, blessed is He, and "Name" signifies tangible grasp
וּבְשַׁבָּת זוֹכִין לְתַקֵּן הַגּוּף שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ תְּפִיסָה מָה בְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בִּסְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית: לְמֶחֱזֵי זִיו דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין,
for on Shabbos we merit to refine the body so that it attains some grasp of the Name Havayah, blessed is He, as we recite at the Third Meal, "to behold the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin,"
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא: נוֹדָע בַּשְּׁעָרִים בַּעְלָהּ — לְפוּם מַה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִיבֵּיהּ
and along the lines of what is brought, "'Her husband is known in the gates'—according to the measure one assesses in his heart"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א' ק"ג רֵישׁ ע"ב).
(Zohar, Vol. 1, 103, top of amud b).
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים אַחַר כָּךְ: הָאֵל בְּתַעֲצוּמוֹת עֻזֶּךָ
And this is why we recite afterward [in the morning Shabbos/Yom Tov liturgy]: "The God in the mighty strengths of Your might (uzecha)"
אֵין עֹז אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
"might (oz) means nothing other than Torah"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' רס"ט סוֹף ע"א),
(Zohar, Vol. 3, 269, end of amud a),
וְלֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְתַבְּרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא
and "there is nothing capable of breaking the evil inclination except Torah"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א' ר"ב.)
(Zohar, Vol. 1, 202a)
בְּתַעֲצוּמוֹת עֻזֶּךָ, שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִתְגַּבֵּר וּמִתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם, וּבְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְגַּבְּרִין עָלָיו: אִם אֶבֶן הוּא נִימּוֹחַ וְכוּלֵּי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוּכָּה

"in the mighty strengths of Your might," for the evil inclination grows stronger and renews itself every day, yet through words of Torah we overpower it—"if it is of stone, it dissolves, etc."—as they said in Sukkah
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַזְכִּיר מִדּוֹת הַגָּדוֹל, הַגִּבּוֹר, וְהַנּוֹרָא, כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת:
And afterward it mentions the attributes "the Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome," corresponding to the holiness of the three Patriarchs:
גְּדוּלָּה וּגְבוּרָה — אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, וְנוֹרָא — יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, אִישׁ תָּם, גְּבַר שְׁלִים
Greatness (Gedulah) and Might (Gevurah) correspond to Avraham and Yitzchak, while Awesome (Nora) corresponds to our father Yaakov, "a wholesome man," a complete person
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ע"ט.),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 79a),
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא
and this is based on what is brought
(ibid. 204a):
ש' רָזָא דִּתְלַת אֲבָהָן, בַּת מִתְעַטֶּרֶת בְּהוּ.
"Shin is the secret of the three Patriarchs, and the Daughter (Bas) is crowned with them."
וְאָמַר: הַגָּדוֹל בִּכְבוֹד שְׁמֶךָ
And it states: "the Great in the glory of Your Name"
"גָּדוֹל" בְּלֹא תַּכְלִית, לְמַעְלָה מֵהַתְּפִיסָה, שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן;
"Great" without limit, transcending all grasp, the Supernal Intellect concealed from all human thought;
"בִּכְבוֹד שְׁמֶךָ" — עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ, כָּבוֹד תַּתָּאָה,
while "in the glory of Your Name" follows what they said, "Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom," the Lower Glory (Malchus),
וְהַיְינוּ מְהֵימְנוּתָא שְׁלֵימְתָא שֶׁהַשְּׁבָטִים הִשִּׂיגוּ עַל יְדֵי הָאֱמוּנָה יִחוּד הֲוָיָ"ה, וְהַיְינוּ מְהֵימְנוּתָא שְׁלֵימְתָא
which is "complete faith," for the tribes grasped the unity of Havayah through faith, which is complete faith
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר כ"ה);
(as explained in Maamar 25);
הַגִּבּוֹר לָנֶצַח — אֵיזֶהוּ גִּבּוֹר? הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ,
"the Mighty forever"—"Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination,"
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים עוֹמֵד עָלָיו, וּמִדַּת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, פַּחַד יִצְחָק, שֶׁהוּא תָּמִיד כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,

which occurs when one perceives that the King of kings stands over him, embodying the attribute of our father Yitzchak, peace be upon him, "the Fear of Yitzchak," standing constantly as if before the King
וְזֶהוּ "גִּבּוֹר לָנֶצַח", גְּבוּרָה עִילָּאָה נָפְקָא מִבִּינָה
and this is "Mighty forever," Supernal Gevurah emerging from Binah
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' קע"ה:)
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 175b)
וּבְתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר
and in Tikkunei Zohar
(תִּיקּוּן מ"ח):
(Tikkun 48):
זַכָּאָה מַאן דְּעָבֵיד לוֹן דִּירָה בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִיבָּא וְאִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתַּמָּן;
"Fortunate is he who makes a dwelling for them in the two chambers of the heart so that the evil inclination is removed from there";
וְהַנּוֹרָא בְּנוֹרְאוֹתֶיךָ — זֶה שְׁלֵימוּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ "בַּיִת", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים
and "the Awesome in Your awesome deeds"—this is the perfection of our father Yaakov, who called the Temple "a House," as they said in Pesachim
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר קָבוּעַ לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא תָּלָה כְּלָל בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עַצְמוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
meaning that it remained permanently established forevermore because he did not rely at all on his own efforts, as it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית מ"ח, ט"ו):
(Bereishis 48:15):
הָאֱלֹהִים הָרֹעֶה אֹתִי מֵעוֹדִי עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה
"The God Who shepherds me from my very beginning until this day"

שֶׁעַל אֲבוֹתָיו אָמַר: אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלְּכוּ אֲבֹתַי לְפָנָיו, שֶׁהֵם הָלְכוּ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם: אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ בְּמִדַּת אַהֲבָה, וְיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ בְּמִדָּתוֹ פַּחַד יִצְחָק, וְעַל עַצְמוֹ אָמַר שֶׁהַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה שֶׁלּוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ,

for regarding his forefathers he said "before Whom my fathers walked," as they walked through their own spiritual exertion—Avraham with his attribute of love, and Yitzchak with his attribute of the Fear of Yitzchak—whereas regarding himself he declared that even his awe and fear came directly from Hashem, may He be blessed,
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: וְהַנּוֹרָא בְּנוֹרְאוֹתֶיךָ;
and this is what we say: "and the Awesome in Your awesome deeds";
הַמֶּלֶךְ הַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רָם וְנִשָּׂא — עַתִּיק יוֹמִין יְתִב,
"the King Who sits upon a high and lofty throne"—"the Ancient of Days sat,"
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי נִתְעַלָּה וְיָשַׁב עַל כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדוֹ, וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: רָם וְנִשָּׂא
and this is what we recite [in Shabbos Shacharis], "On the seventh day He ascended and sat upon His throne of glory," which is "high and lofty"
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ וְנַעֲשִׂים מִקְדָּשׁ וּמִשְׁכָּן שֶׁנִּקְרָא הֲדוֹם רַגְלֵי אֱלֹהֵינוּ, וְכָאָמוּר.
and this happens when Israel accept the yoke of His kingship and become a Sanctuary and Tabernacle, which is called "the footstool of our God," as stated.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yosef Chaim of Baghdad, Ben Yehoyada, Berachos 7a — “‘Yishmael My son, bless Me’: in its plain sense this is like ‘He who is gracious to the poor lends to Hashem’: one who asks for the good of Israel is regarded as though he blesses Him. As the Nefesh HaChaim explains, blessing means increase in the holy Sefiros alluded to in the letters of His Names: the one who blesses causes light to pour forth from His very Essence into His holy Sefiros and the holy worlds, and since the Sefiros are bound to Him, the blessing is ascribed to Him. And ‘He nodded to me with His head’ alludes to the descent of flow from the first three Sefiros, called His head: his prayer bore fruit at once.” Connection: Ben Yehoyada also reads ‘bless Me’ as a call to draw blessing down from the highest source into the worlds and onto Israel, and adds the mechanism of increase in the Sefiros and the nod as flow from the uppermost three.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 202a (Mikeitz) — "We learned: A person should always stir up his good inclination against his evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, good; if not, let him engage in Torah, for there is nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it."

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52b — "The school of R. Yishmael taught: If this repulsive one [the evil inclination] meets you, drag him to the study hall. If he is stone, he will melt; if iron, he will shatter. 'If stone, he will melt' — as it says, 'Ho, all who thirst, go to the water,' and 'Water wears away stones.'" Just before: "A person's inclination overpowers him every day."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 79a (Yisro) — "What is 'for it is awesome (nora)'? R. Elazar said: the completeness of all, as it says, 'the great, the mighty and the awesome God.' What is 'the awesome'? This is Yaakov, and it is written, 'Yaakov was a tam,' which the Targum renders 'a complete man' (gevar shelim) — complete in everything."

Shin is the secret of the three Avos, who unite with the only daughter (bas), and she is crowned with them."

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 88a — "'Let us go up to the mountain of Hashem, to the house of the God of Yaakov': not the God of Avraham and Yitzchak, but of Yaakov — not like Avraham, of whom 'mountain' is written, nor like Yitzchak, of whom 'field' is written, but like Yaakov, who called it 'house,' as it says, 'He called the name of that place Beis El.'" Rashi: mountain, field and house all refer to the Temple Mount, where they prayed.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 8 — “‘The awesome’ corresponds to Yaakov, who said: ‘The God before whom my fathers walked’: they served by their own effort, each at his level, and of himself he said, ‘The God who has shepherded me,’ that he has nothing through his own effort, only what Hashem shines to him and shepherds him… Fear that comes from a person’s side, setting in his heart before Whom he stands, may not endure, for a person’s inclination grows strong against him every day. But Yaakov’s trait, where awe falls on him from Hashem’s side, endures for ever.” Connection: It gives the same reading of ‘the awesome’ as Yaakov’s fear that comes from Hashem and so lasts, and adds that this is why ‘U’vechen ten pachdecha’ was set in the blessing of Yaakov.
